# Pilot — UK Contracts Finder

**Real data, not a fixture.** Generated by `tools/adapters/ocds.py` from the live
[UK Contracts Finder](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk) OCDS endpoint — a national
government publisher, outside the US, that had never heard of schemaGov.

```bash
python3 tools/adapters/ocds.py \
  --url "https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Published/Notices/OCDS/Search?limit=50" \
  --base "https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/id" \
  --out examples/pilot-uk-contracts
```

50 releases → 49 contracting processes, 40 buyer organizations, 45 supplier parties.

## What it found

Nine profiles built against one self-authored example city validated perfectly. Real data
from one publisher broke the schema in two places within minutes — **both of them my error,
not the publisher's.**

### `areaServed` was wrongly required on every organization

`_core` required a government organization to declare the territory it governs, reasoning that
a body with no territory cannot be placed in the hierarchy. That is right for a publisher
describing *their own* org chart, and wrong for an organization *referenced from another
profile*. Contracts Finder names "Northumberland County Council" as a buyer; it does not
restate which territory that council governs, because that lives in a different register.

**40 real UK buyers could not be represented at all.** The requirement moved from the schema
to Standard conformance: identity is enough at Core, territorial placement is required of
publishers claiming Standard.

### `procurementMethod` was wrongly required on every tender

The transparency argument is sound — without it, *how much public spending was never
competed* is unanswerable. But enforcing it in the schema meant four real notices could not be
represented. Same fix: optional at Core, required at Standard.

### Scheme provenance was being overstated

The adapter initially labelled every OCDS scheme as `org-id:`, but `GB-CFS` and `GB-SRS` are
Contracts Finder's internal registers, not entries in the curated
[org-id.guide](https://org-id.guide). Since the entire point of scheme-qualified identity is
knowing which register a code came from, `local:` now marks a publisher's own scheme:

```
org-id:GB-COH   21   Companies House          (registered)
org-id:GB-GOR    2   Government Organisations (registered)
local:GB-CFS    52   Contracts Finder         (publisher-internal)
local:GB-SRS    10   Supplier Registration    (publisher-internal)
```

## The conformance ladder, working as designed

This data validates at **Core**. Claiming **Standard** fails with 40 specific, actionable
reasons — every organization missing its `areaServed`. That is exactly what the ladder in
[SPEC §4](../../SPEC.md#4-validation) was for: real data can be represented and published
today, and the bar for claiming more is enforced rather than asserted.

## Source fields with no schemaGov mapping

Reported by the adapter rather than silently dropped:

| Field | Count | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `award.documents` | 45 | Award notices and contract documents |
| `award.datePublished` | 45 | Distinct from `award.date` |
| `tender.documents` | 4 | |
| `tender.additionalClassifications` | 4 | Secondary CPV codes |
| `tender.minValue` | 3 | Lower bound of an estimate range |

None are modelled yet. `documents` is the clearest candidate for the next revision.
